cards.text: Jesus just told a crowd about a rich man who planned bigger barns for all his stuff, until God said his life would be required of him that very night. Now Jesus turns to His disciples and says, “Therefore I tell you, do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will wear.” Friend, for YEARS worrying was my whole personality.

cards.question: Jesus gives the disciples His first reason not to worry. What is it?

cards.text: Then Jesus says to consider the ravens: they don't sow or reap, and they have no storehouse or barn. No barn, no apron, no oven timer, and that bird STILL worries less than I ever did.

cards.question: Jesus says the ravens go hungry because they have no storehouse or barn.
God feeds the ravens, and Jesus says the disciples are much more ___ than the birds.

cards.text: Then Jesus asks, “Who of you by worrying can add a single hour to his life?” I worried in the back of a junk drawer for YEARS, friend, and all it ever added was dust.

cards.question: Jesus calls adding a single hour to your life by worrying a small thing.
Nobody can add even one hour to his life by worrying. So what does Jesus ask the disciples?

answers.text: Why ask God for more time

cards.text: Now Jesus says to consider how the lilies grow: they don't labor or spin. No job, no boss, no clocking in, and they STILL look better than me in this hat.

cards.question: Jesus says not even King ___ in all his glory was adorned like one of these lilies.

cards.text: Then Jesus says if that is how God clothes the grass of the field, which is here today and tomorrow is thrown into the furnace… Here today, furnace tomorrow, and that's every batch I ever forgot the timer on.

cards.question: If God clothes grass that is gone by tomorrow, what does Jesus say God will do for the disciples?
Right after that promise, Jesus praises the disciples for their great faith.

cards.text: Jesus comes back around: don't be concerned about what you'll eat or drink. Don't worry about it, He says, and I think by now the disciples are getting the message LOUD and clear.

cards.question: Jesus says the Gentiles of the world strive after food and drink. What does He say about the disciples' Father?

answers.text: He wants them to strive harder
He will make them wait first

cards.question: Instead of striving after all these things, what does Jesus tell the disciples to seek?
Jesus says that if the disciples seek His kingdom, these things will be added unto them.

cards.text: Then Jesus calls the disciples “little flock” and tells them not to be afraid. I've been called a lot of things, friend, but with this mustache, little has NEVER been one of them.

cards.question: Jesus tells His little flock not to be afraid, because their Father is pleased to give them the ___.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells them to sell their possessions and give to the poor. Back in the junk drawer, all I owned was dust, and NOBODY was buying.

cards.question: Jesus tells the disciples to provide themselves with purses that will not wear out. What else does He tell them to provide themselves?
Jesus says no thief can approach that treasure in heaven, but a moth still can.
Jesus gives one more reason. He says that where your treasure is, something else will be there also. What is it?

cards.text: And that's where we'll leave it for now. Keep your apron on, friend, because Jesus isn't done teaching.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "Why not worry even more" is silly. Jesus has just spent four verses saying not to worry, so no baker would pick it. It also doesn't match the tone of the other answers, which leaves effectively two real choices.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The only joke here is "getting the message LOUD and clear." It's a stock phrase, not a real laugh. The card reads like a nice dad being pleasant.

rule.text: If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.

findings.problem: The question says the Gentiles strive after "food and drink." Luke 12:30 says they strive after "all these things," which in context can include the clothing from 12:22-28. The paraphrase narrows what the text calls them.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The question asks what Jesus tells the disciples to seek, and the right answer is "His kingdom." With Jesus as the subject, "His" reads as Jesus' kingdom. In Luke 12:31, "His" points back to "your Father" in 12:30, which was on the previous card and is no longer on screen. The question should say whose kingdom, for example "the Father's kingdom." Card 4 repeats "His kingdom" with the same problem.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question asks what ELSE Jesus tells them to provide besides purses, which makes the purses and the treasure two separate things. In Luke 12:33, "an inexhaustible treasure in heaven" stands right beside "purses that will not wear out" with no "and." The text doesn't say they are separate, so the question decides how the two connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The continuation line opens with "And that's where we'll leave it for now," copied word for word from the doc's example line.

rule.text: The examples show the idea. Write your own line each time.

findings.problem: This card is only the "story isn't over" line and tells no verse, but it cites Luke 12:34, which card 10 already asked about. The citation rule says a story card cites the verses it tells, and the schema requires a verses value.
findings.question: When the last story card is only the "story isn't over" line and tells no verse, what should its "verses" field cite: the passage's last verse, the whole passage, or something else?
